implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2022) was revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). The privileged access and vendor access procedures under it are being written.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud identity provider (SOC 2 Type 2); ERP vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Accounts are created in the directory from the HR feed and synchronized to the cloud identity provider. Outage contractor accounts are created in bulk with an end date. Gaps: access reviews are annual (last January 2026), not quarterly; transfers do not remove prior WMS roles; P07 found 6 of 25 sampled outage contractor accounts still enabled 30 days after the 2025 outage ended.
evidence: HR feed configuration; directory and identity provider exports; access review record January 2026

implementation_statement: Lifecycle automation in the identity provider disables accounts on the HR termination date.
Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled by a scheduled directory job.

WMS, CAP, and EDMS use role-based access from directory groups. EDMS restricted folders hold Security-Related Information (SRI). Gap: SRI-marked documents were found on general engineering shares (gap 9).
evidence: WMS role catalog (41 roles); EDMS restricted folder list; P03 share sample
regulatory_driver: C-NUCLEAR-S01 (73.22 practices applied to SRI by company policy); S06

implementation_statement: The business network cannot initiate any connection to Level 3 or Level 4; plant data arrives only through the one-way deterministic device (CSP). Inside Level 2, flows are not restricted between server groups (gap 2).
evidence: Firewall rule export; CSP defensive architecture drawing (SRI); P07 reachability test

implementation_statement: WMS clearance approval requires a different user from the preparer; GDSR script changes need a second reviewer (planned, gap 12).
Standard users have no local administrator rights. Gap: 16 standing domain administrator accounts (14 IT staff, 2 vendor accounts) (gap 1).
IT staff have separate administrator accounts, but these are used for email on 3 of 14 sampled administrators (P07).
Cloud console administration uses just-in-time elevation through the broker. On-premises directory, WMS, and database administrators have standing access (gap 1).
Cloud privileged sessions are logged. Directory and database administrator actions are logged locally but not reviewed or sent to the SIEM (gap 6).
Lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based throttling in the identity provider; directory lockout after 10 attempts.
Logon banner states monitoring and authorized use on all business network devices and the VPN.
Screens lock after 15 minutes; 5 minutes on shared work control center workstations.
Sessions end after 12 hours or on risk signal.
Workforce remote access uses the VPN with MFA and device checks. Gap: the WMS vendor and the predictive maintenance vendor use 2 shared vendor VPN accounts that stay enabled (gap 4).
regulatory_driver: C-NUCLEAR-R04 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 6, for the dispatch network); S06

implementation_statement: VPN sessions are logged and sent to the SIEM; vendor sessions are not recorded.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: VPN uses TLS 1.2 or higher with approved ciphers.
Corporate Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with certificates; guest Wi-Fi is internet-only. No wireless in the protected area connects to the business network (CSP restriction).

Laptops and tablets are managed and encrypted. Rugged field tablets are used only at Level 2 and are labeled; the CSP prohibits moving them to Levels 3 or 4. 2 of 20 sampled tablets lacked the Level 2 label (P07).
Use of personal devices is limited to email and chat through the managed app. External cloud storage is not blocked.
Training requirements are in POL-01 and POL-05; reviewed annually.

Annual awareness training for employees and long-term contractors (97% completion) and phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 5.9%). Outage contractors receive a 20-minute module at in-processing that does not cover SRI handling or PMMD rules.
Insider threat awareness is part of the annual module and the 73.56 behavioral observation training.
IT administrators receive role training; no specific training on the CSP boundary for IT staff since 2023.
Logging requirements are stated in POL-03; the logging standard (STD-02) is in draft.

Directory, identity provider, VPN, firewall, EDR, and cloud audit logs are collected. Not collected: WMS, EDMS, and CAP application logs, the one-way device receive server, and database audit logs (gap 6).
Collected logs include user, time, source, event, and outcome.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews and correlates alerts 24x7. No review of application logs or of attempts to reach Level 3 boundary addresses (gap 6).
Automated correlation in the MSSP-operated SIEM.
All business systems synchronize to internal time servers that use a GPS reference.
SIEM data is write-protected; cloud audit logs go to a locked bucket in the shared services account.
SIEM retains 1 year searchable. Security-relevant records that support CSP evidence are not identified for longer retention (73.54(h) needs retention until license termination for CSP records).
Audit generation is enabled on servers and network devices; WMS and CAP application auditing is enabled but not forwarded.
Assessment policy is part of POL-01; annual independent assessment.
Annual control assessment by the co-sourced internal audit firm with Nuclear Oversight (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21).
Interconnection agreements exist for the cloud provider, MSSP, and PPA-2 data portal. Gaps: no written interconnection terms for the WMS vendor VPN or the predictive maintenance gateway.
POA&M maintained (P07) and reported to the audit committee each quarter.
Internal operating decision by the Site Vice President, 2026-09-17, with conditions (section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring through the SIEM, EDR, cloud posture service, and quarterly scans. No metrics report to management beyond incident counts.

Annual external and internal penetration test of the business network (last 2026-03). Tailored in (High baseline control) because the business network borders the CSP boundary. The test confirmed no path to Level 3.
Configuration management is covered in POL-01; the configuration standard (STD-01) is in draft.
Gold images for workstations and laptops; no documented server baselines (gap; P07).

Change advisory board for infrastructure and WMS changes. GDSR meter-data scripts and analytics feeds change without tickets (gap 12). Changes that touch Level 3 data flows are not routed to the CST (gap 3).
Security impact analysis is a field on change tickets but is often blank (P07: 9 of 25 sampled).
Only infrastructure administrators can change servers; WMS configuration rights limited to 4 named administrators.
Workstation settings enforced by group policy. Server hardening is not benchmarked (P07: 4 of 10 sampled servers below 70% of benchmark).
Unneeded services removed from gold images; legacy SMBv1 still enabled on the 2 clearance servers for the tag printers.

Asset inventory from EDR and device management for endpoints and servers; network devices and the one-way device receive server management interfaces are incomplete (P07 found an unmanaged server management interface).
Inventory is updated when devices are enrolled; not reconciled with the purchase records.
Software licensing tracked by procurement and IT.
Users cannot install software; requests go through the service desk.
Contingency policy statements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is in draft.
An IT disaster recovery plan exists for the site data center with a cloud pilot-light design for WMS and CAP/EDMS. It does not reflect the BIA RTOs (P05) or the manual 73.77(b) CAP fallback (gap 5).
The IT DR plan was coordinated with Work Management and Operations in 2023, not with Emergency Preparedness or the CST.
Contingency training for IT staff and process owners is planned after STD-07 is issued.
No failover test of the pilot-light DR. Only file share restores have been tested (gap 5). First WMS failover test scheduled 2026-11-14.
Backups are stored in the cloud recovery account in a second region.
Pilot-light environment for WMS and CAP/EDMS in the recovery account. The clearance module cannot run there until it moves off Windows Server 2012 R2 (gap 10).
Dual internet circuits from different carriers at the Station; single circuit at the EOF (P01 R-044).
Daily backups of on-premises servers and cloud workloads to the recovery account with 35-day write-once retention and separate credentials.
Monthly file share restore test; no application-level restore test for WMS, CAP, EDMS, or RWP.
Rebuild procedures exist for workstations and file servers; none for WMS, the clearance module, or CAP (gap 5).
Identification and authentication policy in POL-02.
Unique IDs for all users, including outage contractors; shared accounts prohibited except the 2 vendor VPN accounts (gap 4).
MFA for privileged accounts through the identity provider and the VPN. Directory administrator logons on the site data center console do not require MFA.
evidence: Conditional access policy; console logon test

implementation_statement: MFA for all users for email, cloud applications, and remote access.
Push MFA with number matching resists replay. Phishing-resistant authenticators for administrators are planned (gap 1).
Corporate Wi-Fi uses device certificates; wired ports in the administration building do not use network access control.
Identifiers are not reused; outage contractor IDs carry an outage prefix.
14-character minimum with a banned password list. Service account passwords for WMS and the historian replica have not been rotated since 2023.
Non-organizational users (PPA-2 buyer staff) use the buyer data portal, not company accounts; vendor users are named except the 2 shared VPN accounts.
Incident response policy POL-03 revised 2026-09-17 to integrate the IT plan with the CSP incident response (gap 7).
MSSP and IT security staff trained; CST trained under the CSP; no joint training since 2024.
Joint IT and CST drill last held 2024-02. CIP-003-9 low-impact plan test held 2024-06 (due again by 2027-06).
MSSP contains endpoints with EDR. Escalation to the CST and the Shift Manager for a suspected pivot toward Level 3 is not written into the IT plan (gap 7).
Incidents tracked in the service management tool; cyber security program deficiencies also entered in the CAP.
Staff report to the service desk or the MSSP. The 73.77 reportability decision belongs to the Shift Manager with the CST; the IT plan does not call them (gap 7).
MSSP incident response retainer; forensic firm through the insurer panel.
IT incident response plan (2023) exists. P08 runbooks issued 2026-09-17 replace the separate procedures; tabletop scheduled 2026-11-05.
Server and network maintenance through change control.
Vendor remote maintenance through VPN with shared accounts (gap 4); not recorded.
Media protection policy in POL-04.
SRI paper and media are controlled by the EDMS restricted process; USB storage is allowed on business laptops with EDR scanning.
Drives are wiped or destroyed with certificates.
Removable media is scanned by EDR on business laptops. Media for Levels 3 and 4 must pass the PMMD kiosk (CSP).
regulatory_driver: C-NUCLEAR-R01 (RG 5.71 B.1.19); C-NUCLEAR-R04 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 5.3); S06

implementation_statement: Physical security policy for the owner-controlled area and the site data center is part of the Station physical protection program.
Site data center access list approved by the IT Director; badges issued by Security.
Site data center is in the administration building inside the owner-controlled area with badge access and video. EOF network room uses a keyed lock (P01 R-046).
Security monitors badge alarms and video for the site data center.
Planning policy in POL-01.
This SSP, version 1.0, 2026-09-17.
Acceptable use policy POL-05 acknowledged annually and at contractor in-processing.
Security architecture for Level 2 is documented with the CSP defensive architecture; the business network internal segmentation design is not (gap 2).
Information security program plan approved by the CEO (POL-01 and the FY2027 roadmap). Tailored in: not in the Moderate baseline.
Risk management strategy with risk appetite statements approved by the CEO 2026-09-17 (P01). Tailored in.
Personnel security for business network users relies on HR screening; for staff with electronic access that could affect safety, security, or EP, on the 73.56 program.

All employees are screened at hire. IT administrators of systems that support EP functions (EOF LAN, ERO callout administration) are not in the 73.56 program because those systems were never evaluated (gap 3).
Terminations disable identity provider access on the HR date. P07 found 2 of 25 sampled terminations with local server accounts still enabled.
Transfers do not remove prior WMS roles (P07: 5 of 25 sampled).
Confidentiality and acceptable use agreements signed at hire and contractor in-processing.
Contractor and vendor security terms exist for outage contractors; business IT vendors lack security addenda (gap 8).
Sanctions under the HR disciplinary policy; 73.56 program actions for behavior of concern.
Risk assessment policy in POL-01.
FIPS 199 categorization in section 6 of this SSP: Moderate.
Enterprise risk assessment per SP 800-30 completed 2026-07-31 (P01, 52 risks).
Supply chain risks of business IT vendors assessed only at onboarding (gap 8).
Quarterly authenticated scans of the business network; no scans of the cloud workloads or the one-way device receive server management interface (P07).
Risk responses recorded in the P01 register and the POA&M.
Critical components identified in the BIA (P05); no supply chain review of them yet.
Security requirements in contracts for CDA suppliers (CSP) but not for business IT purchases (gap 8).
Security engineering principles applied to the Level 2 design: deny by default at the CSP boundary, one-way data flow only.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider; ERP vendor; identity provider; MSSP
implementation_statement: External services listed in section 8; 9 of 24 Tier 1 vendors have no current SOC 2 or equivalent on file (gap 8).
2 clearance servers on Windows Server 2012 R2 (gap 10) with compensating controls: isolated VLAN planned, EDR installed, extended security updates purchased.
Carrier DDoS protection on both Station circuits; cloud edge protection for the GDSR application.
Internet edge firewalls and the CSP boundary (one-way device into Level 2) are strong; internal Level 2 segmentation is missing (gap 2).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default at the internet edge and the CSP boundary; allow-all inside the server VLAN.
TLS 1.2 or higher for applications and the site-to-cloud VPN; the PPA-2 data portal uses mutual TLS.
Company-managed keys in the cloud key service; separate keys for the recovery account.
FIPS-validated cryptographic modules where available.
Full-disk encryption on laptops and tablets; storage encryption for servers and cloud workloads.
Monthly patching; P07 found 6 of 40 sampled critical findings past the 30-day target, all on WMS and clearance servers.
EDR on all managed endpoints and servers with 24x7 MSSP monitoring.
evidence: EDR console; P07 test (5 of 5 detected)

implementation_statement: SIEM and EDR monitoring. Gaps: no application logs, no alert on attempts to reach Level 3 boundary addresses (gap 6).
Advisories from CISA, the E-ISAC, and vendors reviewed weekly; the CST receives NRC and industry advisories for CDAs.
File integrity monitoring on the one-way device receive server is planned; WMS clearance records have database constraints but no integrity check against tampering.
Email filtering with attachment sandboxing.
GDSR validates hourly data ranges against meter limits; no checks on manual adjustments (gap 12).
Records retention schedule covers business records; CSP records follow 73.54(h).
Supply chain policy statements added to POL-01 (2026-09-17); vendor risk standard STD-03 in draft.
A business IT supply chain risk plan will extend the CSP supply chain controls (RG 5.71 C.12) to Tier 1 business vendors.
Supply chain controls for CDA purchases under the CSP; none for business IT purchases.
Approved purchase channels for servers and network gear; not documented as a strategy.
Tier 1 vendor assessments at onboarding only; annual SOC 2 review program starting (P09).
Hardware bought from authorized resellers; counterfeit controls for safety-related parts are in the quality program.
